pairs: Nuntiatum est autem Joab quod rex fleret et lugeret filium suum,
Now it was reported to Joab that the king was weeping and mourning for his son.
et versa est victoria in luctum in die illa omni populo:
And so the victory on that day was turned into mourning for all the people.
audivit enim populus in die illa dici:
For the people heard it said on that day,
Dolet rex super filio suo.
“The king is grieving over his son.”
Et declinavit populus in die illa ingredi civitatem,
And the people declined to enter the city on that day,
quomodo declinare solet populus versus et fugiens de prælio.
in the manner that the people were accustomed to decline if they had turned and fled from battle.
Porro rex operuit caput suum,
And the king covered his head,
et clamabat voce magna: Fili mi Absalom,
and he was crying out in a great voice: “My son,
Absalom fili mi,
Absalom! Absalom, my son,
fili mi.
my son!”
Ingressus ergo Joab ad regem in domum,
Therefore, Joab, entering to the king in the house,
dixit:
said:
Confudisti hodie vultus omnium servorum tuorum, qui salvam fecerunt animam tuam,
“Today you have shamed the faces of all your servants, who saved your life,
et animam filiorum tuorum et filiarum tuarum,
and the lives of your sons and your daughters,
et animam uxorum tuarum,
and the lives of your wives,
et animam concubinarum tuarum.
and the lives of your concubines.
Diligis odientes te,
You love those who hate you,
et odio habes diligentes te:
and you hate those who love you.
et ostendisti hodie quia non curas de ducibus tuis et de servis tuis:
And you have revealed this day that you have no concern for your leaders and for your servants.
et vere cognovi modo,
And truly,
quia si Absalom viveret,
I know now that if Absalom had lived,
et omnes nos occubuissemus,
and if we all had been killed,
tunc placeret tibi.
then it would have pleased you.
Nunc igitur surge, et procede,
Now then, rise up and go out,
et alloquens satisfac servis tuis:
and speak so as to make amends to your servants.
juro enim tibi per Dominum quod si non exieris,
For I swear to you by the Lord that if you will not go forth,
ne unus quidem remansurus sit tecum nocte hac:
not even one person will be left with you this night.
et pejus erit hoc tibi quam omnia mala quæ venerunt super te ab adolescentia tua usque in præsens.
And this will be worse for you than all the evils that have come to you, from your youth even to the present.”
Surrexit ergo rex et sedit in porta:
Therefore, the king rose up, and he sat at the gate.
et omni populo nuntiatum est quod rex sederet in porta.
And it was announced to all the people that the king was sitting at the gate.
Venitque universa multitudo coram rege:
And the entire multitude went before the king.
Israël autem fugit in tabernacula sua.
But Israel fled to their own tents.
Omnis quoque populus certabat in cunctis tribubus Israël,
And all the people were conflicted, in all the tribes of Israel,
dicens:
saying:
Rex liberavit nos de manu inimicorum nostrorum;
“The king has freed us from the hand of our enemies.
ipse salvavit nos de manu Philisthinorum:
He himself saved us from the hand of the Philistines.
et nunc fugit de terra propter Absalom.
But now he flees from the land for the sake of Absalom.
Absalom autem,
But Absalom,
quem unximus super nos,
whom we anointed over us,
mortuus est in bello:
has died in the war.
usquequo siletis,
How long will you be silent,
et non reducitis regem?
and not lead back the king?”
Rex vero David misit ad Sadoc et Abiathar sacerdotes,
Then truly, king David sent to Zadok and Abiathar, the priests,
dicens:
saying:
Loquimini ad majores natu Juda, dicentes:
“Speak to those greater by birth of Judah, saying:
Cur venitis novissimi ad reducendum regem in domum suam?
‘Why have you arrived last to lead back the king into his house?
(Sermo autem omnis Israël pervenerat ad regem in domo ejus.)
(For the talk in all of Israel had reached the king in his house.)
Fratres mei vos,
You are my brothers;
os meum,
you are my bone
et caro mea vos,
and my flesh.
quare novissimi reducitis regem?
Why are you the last to lead back the king?’
Et Amasæ dicite: Nonne os meum,
And say to Amasa: ‘Are you not my bone and my flesh?
et caro mea es?
May God do these things,
hæc faciat mihi Deus, et hæc addat,
and may he add these other things,
si non magister militiæ fueris coram me omni tempore pro Joab.
if you will not be the leader of the military in my sight, for all time, in the place of Joab.’”
Et inclinavit cor omnium virorum Juda quasi viri unius:
And he inclined the heart of all the men of Judah, as if one man.
miseruntque ad regem, dicentes:
And they sent to the king, saying,
Revertere tu, et omnes servi tui.
“Return, you and all your servants.”
Et reversus est rex,
And the king returned.
et venit usque ad Jordanem:
And he went as far as the Jordan,
et omnis Juda venit usque in Galgalam ut occurreret regi,
and all of Judah went as far as Gilgal, so as to meet the king,
et traduceret eum Jordanem.
and to lead him across the Jordan.
Festinavit autem Semei filius Gera filii Jemini de Bahurim, et descendit cum viris Juda in occursum regis David,
And Shimei, the son of Gera, the son of Benjamin, from Bahurim, hurried and descended with the men of Judah to meet king David,
cum mille viris de Benjamin,
with one thousand men from Benjamin,
et Siba puer de domo Saul:
and with Ziba,
et quindecim filii ejus,
the servant from the house of Saul.
ac viginti servi erant cum eo:
And with him were his fifteen sons
et irrumpentes Jordanem,
and twenty servants.
ante regem
And going into the Jordan,
transierunt vada,
they crossed the fords before the king,
ut traducerent domum regis,
so that they might lead across the house of the king,
et facerent juxta jussionem ejus:
and might act in accord with his order. Then, Shimei,
Semei autem filius Gera prostratus coram rege, cum jam transisset Jordanem,
the son of Gera, prostrating himself before the king after he had now gone across the Jordan,
dixit ad eum:
said to him:
Ne reputes mihi,
“May you not impute to me,
domine mi,
my lord,
iniquitatem,
the iniquity,
neque memineris injuriarum servi tui in die qua egressus es,
nor call to mind the injuries,
domine mi rex,
of your servant in the day that you,
de Jerusalem,
my lord the king,
neque ponas,
departed from Jerusalem.
rex,
And may you not store it up in your heart,
in corde tuo.
O king.
Agnosco enim servus tuus peccatum meum:
For as your servant, I acknowledge my sin. And for this reason,
et idcirco hodie primus veni de omni domo Joseph,
today, I arrive as the first from all the house of Joseph,
descendique in occursum domini mei regis.
and I descend to meet my lord the king.”
Respondens vero Abisai filius Sarviæ,
Yet truly, Abishai, the son of Zeruiah,
dixit:
responding,
Numquid pro his verbis non occidetur Semei,
said, “Should not Shimei, because of these words,
quia maledixit christo Domini?
be killed, since he cursed the Christ of the Lord?”
Et ait David:
And David said:
Quid mihi et vobis,
“What is it to me and to all of you,
filii Sarviæ?
O sons of Zeruiah?
cur efficimini mihi hodie in satan?
Why are you acting toward me this day like Satan?
ergone hodie interficietur vir in Israël?
Why should any man be put to death on this day in Israel?
an ignoro hodie me factum regem super Israël?
Or do you not know that today I have been made king over Israel?”
Et ait rex Semei:
And the king said to Shimei,
Non morieris.
“You shall not die.”
Juravitque ei.
And he swore to him.
Miphiboseth quoque filius Saul descendit in occursum regis,
And Mephibosheth, the son of Saul, descended to meet the king,
illotis pedibus et intonsa barba:
with unwashed feet and uncut beard.
vestesque suas non laverat a die qua egressus fuerat rex,
And he had not washed his garments from the day that the king had departed,
usque ad diem reversionis ejus in pace.
until the day of his return in peace.
Cumque Jerusalem occurrisset regi,
And when he had met the king at Jerusalem,
dixit ei rex:
the king said to him,
Quare non venisti mecum,
“Why did you not go with me,
Miphiboseth?
Mephibosheth?”
Et respondens ait:
And in response, he said:
Domine mi rex,
“My lord the king,
servus meus contempsit me:
my servant spurned me. And I,
dixique ei ego famulus tuus ut sterneret mihi asinum,
your servant, spoke to him so that he might saddle a donkey for me,
et ascendens abirem cum rege:
and I might climb upon it and go with the king.
claudus enim sum servus tuus.
For I, your servant, am lame.
Insuper et accusavit me servum tuum ad te dominum meum regem: tu autem, domine mi rex, sicut angelus Dei es: fac quod placitum est tibi.
Moreover, he also accused me, your servant, to you, my lord the king. But you, my lord the king, are like an Angel of God. Do whatever is pleasing to you.
Neque enim fuit domus patris mei, nisi morti obnoxia domino meo regi:
For my father’s house was deserving of nothing but death before my lord the king.
tu autem posuisti me servum tuum inter convivas mensæ tuæ:
Yet you have placed me, your servant, among the guests of your table.
quid ergo habeo justæ querelæ?
Therefore, what just complaint might I have?
aut quid possum ultra vociferari ad regem?
Or what else can I cry out to the king?”
Ait ergo ei rex:
Then the king said to him:
Quid ultra loqueris?
“Why are you still speaking?
fixum est quod locutus sum:
What I have spoken is fixed.
tu et Siba dividite possessiones.
You and Ziba shall divide the possessions.”
Responditque Miphiboseth regi:
And Mephibosheth responded to the king,
Etiam cuncta accipiat,
“But now let him take it all,
postquam reversus est dominus meus rex pacifice in domum suam.
since my lord the king has been returned peacefully into his own house.”
Berzellai quoque Galaadites,
Likewise, Barzillai the Gileadite,
descendens de Rogelim,
descending from Rogelim,
traduxit regem Jordanem,
led the king across the Jordan,
paratus etiam ultra fluvium prosequi eum.
having prepared also to follow him beyond the river.
Erat autem Berzellai Galaadites senex valde,
Now Barzillai the Gileadite was very old,
id est,
that is,
octogenarius,
eighty years old.
et ipse præbuit alimenta regi cum moraretur in castris:
And he provided the king with sustenance when he was staying at the encampment.
fuit quippe vir dives nimis.
For indeed, he was an exceedingly rich man.
Dixit itaque rex ad Berzellai:
And so the king said to Barzillai,
Veni mecum,
“Come with me,
ut requiescas securus mecum in Jerusalem.
so that you may rest securely with me in Jerusalem.”
Et ait Berzellai ad regem:
And Barzillai said to the king:
Quot sunt dies annorum vitæ meæ,
“How many days remain in the years of my life,
ut ascendam cum rege in Jerusalem?
that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem?
Octogenarius sum hodie:
Today I am eighty years old.
numquid vigent sensus mei ad discernendum suave aut amarum?
Are my senses quick to discern sweet and bitter?
aut delectare potest servum tuum cibus et potus?
Or is food and drink able to delight your servant?
vel audire possum ultra vocem cantorum atque cantatricum?
Or can I still hear the voice of men and women singers?
quare servus tuus sit oneri domino meo regi?
Why should your servant be a burden to my lord the king?
Paululum procedam famulus tuus ab Jordane tecum:
I, your servant, shall proceed a little ways from the Jordan with you.
non indigeo hac vicissitudine,
I am not in need of this recompense.
sed obsecro ut revertar servus tuus,
But I beg you that I,
et moriar in civitate mea,
your servant,
et sepeliar juxta sepulchrum patris mei
may be returned and may die in my own city,
et matris meæ.
and may be buried beside the sepulcher of my father and my mother.
Est autem servus tuus Chamaam:
But there is your servant Chimham;
ipse vadat tecum,
let him go with you,
domine mi rex,
my lord the king.
et fac ei quidquid tibi bonum videtur.
And do for him whatever seems good to you.”
Dixit itaque ei rex:
And so the king said to him:
Mecum transeat Chamaam,
“Let Chimham cross over with me,
et ego faciam ei quidquid tibi placuerit:
and I will do for him whatever will be pleasing to you.
et omne quod petieris a me,
And all that you ask of me,
impetrabis.
you shall obtain.”
Cumque transisset universus populus et rex Jordanem,
And when the entire people and the king had crossed over the Jordan,
osculatus est rex Berzellai,
the king kissed Barzillai,
et benedixit ei:
and he blessed him.
et ille reversus est in locum suum.
And he returned to his own place.
Transivit ergo rex in Galgalam,
Then the king went on to Gilgal,
et Chamaam cum eo.
and Chimham went with him.
Omnis autem populus Juda traduxerat regem,
Now all the people of Judah had led the king across,
et media tantum pars adfuerat de populo Israël.
but only as much as one half part of the people of Israel were there.
Itaque omnes viri Israël concurrentes ad regem dixerunt ei:
And so, all the men of Israel, running to the king,
Quare te furati sunt fratres nostri viri Juda,
said to him: “Why have our brothers, the men of Judah,
et traduxerunt regem et domum ejus Jordanem,
stolen you away. And why have they led the king and his house across the Jordan,
omnesque viros David cum eo?
and all the men of David with him?”
Et respondit omnis vir Juda ad viros Israël:
And all the men of Judah responded to the men of Israel:
Quia mihi propior est rex:
“Because the king is nearer to me.
cur irasceris super hac re?
Why are you angry over this matter?
numquid comedimus aliquid ex rege,
Have we eaten anything belonging to the king,
aut munera nobis data sunt?
or have any gifts been given to us?”
Et respondit vir Israël ad viros Juda,
And the men of Israel responded to the men of Judah,
et ait:
and said:
Decem partibus major ego sum apud regem,
“I have the greater amount, ten parts, with the king,
magisque ad me pertinet David quam ad te:
and so David belongs to me more so than to you.
cur fecisti mihi injuriam,
Why have you caused me injury,
et non mihi nuntiatum est priori,
and why was it not announced to me first,
ut reducerem regem meum?
so that I might lead back my king?”
Durius autem responderunt viri Juda viris Israël.
But the men of Judah answered more firmly than the men of Israel.
